name: port-design-system-from-local-clone
description: Port a complete visual design system from a local clone into an existing Next.js project. Target keeps content, routes, and backend but looks visually identical to source.
prompt:
# Port Design System From Local Clone

You are about to perform a **FULL VISUAL REPLACEMENT** of a target project using the visual design system from a source project, using the paths provided in `the source path and target path provided by the user`.

Parse `the source path and target path provided by the user` as:
1. `<source-path>` (required — absolute path to local clone with the design)
2. `<target-path>` (required — absolute path to existing Next.js project)
3. `<commit-hash>` (optional — baseline commit in target to restore before porting)

If `<commit-hash>` is provided, run `git stash push -m "pre-port-design-system stash"` then `git checkout <commit-hash>` in target before starting.
If not provided, work with the target's current state.
If `<source-path>` or `<target-path>` is missing, stop and ask for it.
If either path contains spaces, the user should wrap it in quotes.

## THE CORE RULE — Read This First

**FULL VISUAL REPLACEMENT — The target becomes VISUALLY IDENTICAL to the source.**

The source is the **ONLY** source of truth for:
- Every CSS custom property value
- Every font, every font size, every font weight, every letter-spacing value
- Every color, every background, every gradient
- Every layout (grid, flex, spacing, gaps, padding, margins)
- Every animation (GSAP timelines, ScrollTrigger configs, Lenis smooth scroll)
- Every hover state, every focus state, every active state, every transition
- Every responsive breakpoint behavior
- Every parallax effect, every scroll-triggered animation
- Every component visual shell (Navbar, Footer, Hero, Cards, Buttons, Forms, Modals, etc.)
- Every decorative asset (background images, hero videos, SVGs, noise textures, 3D scenes)
- Every box-shadow, border-radius, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode

The target receives **ALL** of the above. Every page, every section, every component, every route — including pages that do NOT exist in the source (Área de Clientes, dashboard, admin pages, etc.). These pages get the full visual treatment using the source's design system.

The ONLY things preserved from the target:
- **Text content** — headings, paragraphs, labels, button text, error messages, everything the user reads
- **Routes** — page file paths, URL structure, dynamic segments, redirects
- **Business logic** — API routes, server actions, database queries, auth flows, form handlers, data fetching, third-party integrations

## Concrete example to eliminate ALL ambiguity:

Source has:
- A Navbar that shrinks on scroll with a background color change, specific hover states, and a hamburger menu that slides from the right
- A hero section with full-screen parallax background, GSAP text reveal on heading with stagger, and a CTA button with glow effect on hover
- Feature cards with 3-column grid, specific border-radius, box-shadow, and scale-up animation on hover
- Footer with specific padding, background color, link styling, and social icons

Target has:
- Different pages (home, products, Área de Clientes, login, dashboard, etc.)
- Different text content (Spanish, different headings, different product names)
- Different routes (/cliente, /login, /dashboard, etc.)

After porting:
- **Navbar** — looks and behaves EXACTLY like source's Navbar (scroll shrink, colors, hover states, hamburger animation). But the links point to target's routes (/cliente, /productos, /login) and auth UI works with target's auth system.
- **Hero** — has the SAME parallax background image from source, SAME GSAP text reveal, SAME CTA button glow. But the heading and subtitle use target's text content.
- **Feature cards** — SAME grid, SAME border-radius, SAME box-shadow, SAME hover animation. But the card content is target's products.
- **Área de Clientes** — receives the FULL visual design system (source's colors, fonts, spacing, button styles, card styles, input styles, animations). It looks like it belongs to the same site as the source. It is NOT "only global tokens" — it gets the COMPLETE visual treatment.
- **Dashboard** — same. Full source design system applied. All dashboard data, charts, and logic preserved. Visual identity is source's.

**Simple test:** Open source and target side by side → they look like the same site (same colors, fonts, spacing, animations, hover effects, scroll behavior). The only difference: target reads differently and goes to different routes.

## Scope Defaults

### Visual Layer — FULLY PORTED to EVERY page of target

Every item in this list is extracted from the source and applied to EVERY page in the target (home, products, contact, Área de Clientes, dashboard, login, legal — ALL of them):

- **CSS custom properties** — every `--token-name: value` in `:root`, `.dark`, and any scope
- **Color palette** — oklch/hex/hsl values for background, foreground, primary, secondary, accent, muted, destructive, border, ring, chart colors, sidebar colors
- **Typography** — font-family declarations, font-weight scale, font-size scale, line-height scale, letter-spacing scale, text-transform patterns
- **Font files** — `.woff2`, `.woff`, `.ttf` files and their `@font-face` declarations or `next/font` configuration
- **Tailwind theme** — colors, spacing, borderRadius, boxShadow, animation, keyframes, screens, fontFamily — everything in `tailwind.config.*` or `@theme` CSS blocks
- **`globals.css`** — all visual tokens, keyframe animations, utility classes, base layer styles
- **GSAP animations** — every `gsap.to()`, `gsap.from()`, `gsap.fromTo()`, `gsap.timeline()` with exact duration, ease, stagger, delay, repeat, yoyo
- **ScrollTrigger configs** — trigger element, start, end, scrub (boolean/number), pin, anticipatePin, toggleActions
- **Lenis smooth scroll** — duration, easing function, smoothWheel, orientation, gestureOrientation, normalizeWheel, wrapper/content selectors
- **Parallax effects** — which elements, speed multiplier, direction, axis, implementation method
- **Hover/focus/active states** — exact transition timing and easing, transform values, color changes, opacity changes, box-shadow changes
- **Responsive breakpoints** — exact pixel values and every CSS property that changes at each breakpoint
- **3D effects** — perspective, rotateX/Y/Z, translateZ, backface-visibility, transform-style
- **Layout patterns** — grid-template-columns/rows, flex configs, gap values, container max-widths, section padding/margin rhythms, aspect ratios
- **Component visual shells** — Navbar (all variants), Footer, Hero, feature cards, testimonial cards, CTA sections, buttons (all states), modals, forms, badges, dividers
- **Decorative assets** — background images, hero videos, SVGs, blob shapes, noise textures, gradient meshes — copied to target's `public/`
- **Box shadows, border radii, opacity patterns, backdrop filters, mix-blend-modes, gradient definitions**
- **Scroll-snap configurations, scroll-driven animations, intersection observer visual triggers**

### Protected Layer — NEVER TOUCHED

- **API routes** — any file under `app/api/` or `pages/api/`
- **Server actions** — any `'use server'` function or file
- **Database** — schemas, ORM models, Prisma, Drizzle, migrations
- **Authentication** — NextAuth, Clerk, session handling, middleware guards
- **Environment** — `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production`, `.env.development`, `.env.test`
- **Text content** — headings, paragraphs, labels, button text, link text, alt text, aria labels, placeholders, error messages, toast messages, meta titles, meta descriptions
- **URL routing** — page file paths, dynamic `[slug]` segments, route groups, `generateStaticParams`, rewrites, redirects
- **Data fetching** — `fetch()`, `useQuery()`, React Query, SWR, tRPC, server component async functions
- **Form handlers** — `action` props, `onSubmit` handlers, validation schemas, FormData processing
- **Third-party integrations** — Google Analytics, GTM, Stripe, HubSpot, Intercom, Sentry, PostHog
- **Business logic** — utilities that process data, calculate prices, format dates, transform API responses
- **Test files** — `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `__tests__/`
- **CI/CD** — `.github/workflows/`, `vercel.json`, deployment configs
- **Package lock** — `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock` (only ADD to `package.json`, never remove)

**The governing rule:** If it affects how the site *works* or what a user *reads* → off-limits. If it affects how the site *looks, moves, or feels* → your responsibility to port it COMPLETELY.

## Pre-Flight

1. **Parse arguments.** Split `the source path and target path provided by the user` into `<source-path>`, `<target-path>`, and optionally `<commit-hash>`. If fewer than 2 paths are provided, ask the user. Resolve relative paths to absolute.

2. **Handle optional commit hash.** If `<commit-hash>` is provided:
   - `cd <target-path>` and `git stash push -m "pre-port stash"`
   - `git checkout <commit-hash>`
   - Verify clean working tree
   - If commit not found: `❌ Commit hash not found: <commit-hash>`. Stop.

3. **Validate source.** Confirm `<source-path>` exists and contains a web project (has `package.json`, CSS files, or HTML files with `<style>`/`<link>`). If not: `❌ Source path not found or not a web project: <source-path>`. Stop.

4. **Validate target.** Confirm `<target-path>` exists and contains a Next.js project (has `next` in `package.json`, has `app/` or `pages/`). If not: `❌ Target path is not a Next.js project: <target-path>`. Stop.

5. **Report findings:**
```
Source: <source-path>
  Framework: <detected>
  Styling: <detected>
  Animation libs: <detected>
  Pages: <list>

Target: <target-path>
  Framework: Next.js (<App Router | Pages Router>)
  Styling: <detected>
  Pages: <list>
  Protected files: <count>
  Baseline commit: <commit-hash or "current HEAD">

Proceeding with full visual replacement...
```

6. **Create working directories.** Create `docs/port-design-system/` in target.

7. **Verify target builds.** `cd <target-path> && npm run build`. If it fails, tell the user to fix first.

## Guiding Principles

### 1. Full Visual Replacement — No Half Measures

You are replacing the ENTIRE visual identity of the target with the source's. Every page, every section, every component, every state. The target becomes visually identical to the source. There is no "only global tokens for some pages." There is no "protect visual shell." The source design system applies to EVERYTHING.

### 2. Target's Text, Routes, and Logic Are Sacred

You change ZERO text content. You change ZERO routes. You change ZERO API routes, server actions, database queries, auth flows, form handlers, data fetching, or business logic. The target's functionality is 100% intact. Only the visual layer is replaced.

### 3. Audit Before You Touch

Read every single file in both projects. You need a complete mental model. 30 minutes of reading saves 3 hours of rework.

### 4. Source Structure Stays, Target Routes Stay

The source's visual structure (grid layouts, section ordering, component hierarchy, spacing scales) is applied to the target. But the target's route structure (file paths, URL segments) is preserved. You are applying the source's design to the target's architecture.

### 5. Install Dependencies, Never Remove Them

Add GSAP, Lenis, font packages, etc. to target's `package.json`. Never remove a target dependency.

### 6. Merge, Don't Replace (for globals.css and config)

The target's `globals.css` may have custom properties the source doesn't define. Merge the source's tokens INTO the target's file, preserving target-specific values. Same for Tailwind config. Every file modification is a surgical merge.

### 7. One Phase, One Verified Build

After each phase, run `npm run build` in the target. A broken build is unacceptable. Fix it completely before moving on.

### 8. Decorative Assets Only

Copy ONLY decorative assets from source (backgrounds, patterns, hero visuals, textures). Never copy content images (product photos, user avatars, blog thumbnails) — those belong to the target.

### 9. Document Every Change

Write `docs/port-design-system/changelog.md` in target. Log every file modified with before → after summary and why.

## Phase 0: Full Source Audit

Read every file in `<source-path>`. Extract everything below into `docs/port-design-system/extraction-report.md` in target.

### CSS Custom Properties
- Every `--token-name: value` in `:root`, `.dark`, and any scope
- File it's declared in

### Typography
- Every `font-family` declaration (CSS and `next/font` config)
- Font weight scale, font size scale, line-height scale, letter-spacing scale
- Font file paths (`.woff2`, `.woff`, `.ttf`)
- `next/font/google` or `next/font/local` imports

### Tailwind Configuration
- `tailwind.config.ts`/`.js` if it exists
- `@theme` blocks in CSS files (Tailwind v4)
- Every custom theme value: colors, spacing, borderRadius, boxShadow, animation, keyframes, screens, fontFamily, fontSize

### Animation Libraries

Search for: `gsap`, `@gsap/react`, `lenis`, `@studio-freight/lenis`, `framer-motion`, `motion`.

**GSAP:**
- Every file that imports `gsap`
- Each animation call: `gsap.to()`, `gsap.from()`, `gsap.fromTo()`, `gsap.timeline()`
- For each: target selector/ref, animated properties and values, duration, ease (exact string), delay, stagger, repeat, yoyo
- Plugin registrations: `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ...)`

**ScrollTrigger:**
- Every `ScrollTrigger.create()` or `scrollTrigger` property
- For each: trigger element, start, end, scrub (boolean/number), pin, anticipatePin, toggleActions, toggleClass

**Lenis:**
- Configuration object: duration, easing function (exact body), smoothWheel, orientation, gestureOrientation, normalizeWheel, infinite
- Where instantiated, RAF integration

### Parallax Effects
- Which elements, speed values (exact numbers), direction, axis, implementation method

### Hover/Focus/Active States
- For each interactive component: which CSS properties change, before/after values, transition property/duration/timing function

### Responsive Breakpoints
- Breakpoint pixel values, what changes at each breakpoint per component, mobile-first or desktop-first

### Component Inventory
Map every component: file path, purely visual vs. business logic, Tailwind classes, animation code, assets referenced.

### Decorative Assets
List every file in source's `public/` that is decorative: background images, hero videos, SVGs, textures, gradient meshes.

### Target Project Mapping
Read every file in `<target-path>`:
- Map all routes: pages, layouts, route groups, dynamic segments
- Map all components: visual styling vs. business logic
- Map all API routes and server actions (untouchable)
- Map auth system (middleware, providers, config)
- Identify current styling approach, animation approach, existing `globals.css` tokens, Tailwind config, font setup

## Phase 0b: Optional Live Source Extraction (MCP)

If source can be run locally or is deployed and browser MCP is available:

1. Navigate to the URL with browser MCP
2. Run these extraction scripts:

**Extract all CSS custom properties:**
```javascript
(function() {
  const root = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const tokens = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < root.length; i++) {
    const prop = root[i];
    if (prop.startsWith('--')) tokens[prop] = root.getPropertyValue(prop).trim();
  }
  return JSON.stringify({ tokens, rootFontSize: root.fontSize, rootLineHeight: root.lineHeight }, null, 2);
})()
```

**Extract computed styles for key elements:**
```javascript
(function() {
  const selectors = ['body','h1','h2','h3','h4','h5','h6','p','a','button','nav','header','footer','input','select','textarea','.hero','.card','.navbar','.cta','.feature'];
  const results = {};
  selectors.forEach(sel => {
    const el = document.querySelector(sel);
    if (!el) return;
    const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
    results[sel] = { fontFamily: cs.fontFamily, fontSize: cs.fontSize, fontWeight: cs.fontWeight, lineHeight: cs.lineHeight, letterSpacing: cs.letterSpacing, color: cs.color, backgroundColor: cs.backgroundColor, padding: cs.padding, margin: cs.margin, gap: cs.gap, borderRadius: cs.borderRadius, boxShadow: cs.boxShadow, transition: cs.transition, transform: cs.transform, maxWidth: cs.maxWidth, display: cs.display, flexDirection: cs.flexDirection, justifyContent: cs.justifyContent, alignItems: cs.alignItems };
  });
  return JSON.stringify(results, null, 2);
})()
```

**Extract GSAP animation timeline data:**
```javascript
(function() {
  if (!window.gsap) return 'GSAP not loaded';
  return JSON.stringify(gsap.globalTimeline.getChildren(true, true, true).map(t => ({
    target: t.target?.nodeType ? t.target.tagName + '.' + t.target.className : String(t.target),
    vars: t.vars, duration: t.duration(), delay: t.delay(), startTime: t.startTime(),
    repeat: t.repeat?.(), yoyo: t.yoyo?.(), ease: t.ease?.name || t.vars?.ease
  })), null, 2);
})()
```

**Extract ScrollTrigger instances:**
```javascript
(function() {
  if (!gsap?.plugins?.ScrollTrigger) return 'ScrollTrigger not loaded';
  return JSON.stringify(ScrollTrigger.getAll().map(st => ({
    trigger: st.trigger?.className || st.trigger?.id || st.trigger?.tagName,
    start: st.vars.start, end: st.vars.end, scrub: st.vars.scrub, pin: st.vars.pin,
    anticipatePin: st.vars.anticipatePin, toggleActions: st.vars.toggleActions
  })), null, 2);
})()
```

**Extract Lenis runtime config:**
```javascript
(function() {
  if (window.lenis) return JSON.stringify({ found: true, options: window.lenis.options }, null, 2);
  if (window.__lenis) return JSON.stringify({ found: true }, null, 2);
  return 'Lenis not found';
})()
```

3. Interaction sweep: hover buttons, scroll full page, resize to 375/768/1024/1440
4. Merge computed values into extraction report — computed values override authored values

This phase is OPTIONAL. Skip if no URL or no browser MCP.

## Phase 1: Global Visual Foundation

Sequential. Do it yourself — do not delegate.

### Step 1: Install Missing Visual Dependencies
Compare source's `package.json` against target's. Install any visual libraries the source uses that the target lacks:
- `gsap` and `@gsap/react`
- `lenis` or `@studio-freight/lenis`
- `framer-motion` or `motion`
- Font packages
- `tailwind-merge`, `clsx`, `class-variance-authority`
- `tw-animate-css` or similar

Never remove target dependencies.

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 2: Merge globals.css
Read source's and target's `globals.css`.

For target's `globals.css`:
- Replace `:root` CSS custom property values with source values
- Same for `.dark` scope
- Port all `@keyframes` from source
- Port `@theme` blocks (Tailwind v4) — merge source theme values
- Port `@layer base` styles that are purely visual

Do NOT remove target CSS that source doesn't override.

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 3: Merge Tailwind Configuration
If source has `tailwind.config.ts`/`.js`:
- Merge each section (colors, spacing, borderRadius, boxShadow, animation, keyframes, screens, fontFamily) into target's config
- Source values override for same key names; target values preserved for keys source doesn't define

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 4: Port Fonts
- If source uses `next/font/google`: add/replace imports in target's `layout.tsx`, apply CSS variables to `<html>` or `<body>`
- If source uses `next/font/local`: copy font files to target's `public/fonts/`, add imports to `layout.tsx`
- Update `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`, `--font-heading` CSS custom properties
- Preserve target's layout.tsx metadata/viewport logic

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 5: Set Up Lenis (if source uses it)
- Create Lenis provider component with exact config from extraction report
- Wire into target's root layout, wrapping `{children}`
- Replicate GSAP ticker integration if source does it

Skip if source doesn't use Lenis.

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 6: Set Up GSAP (if source uses it)
- Create GSAP registration module in target
- Register same plugins (ScrollTrigger, etc.)
- Set same global defaults
- Create provider/context hook if source has one

Skip if source doesn't use GSAP.

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 7: Port Navbar Visual Shell
Read source's Navbar: extract Tailwind classes, layout structure, colors, typography, spacing, hover states, scroll-triggered behavior, hamburger menu animation, logo sizing.

Read target's Navbar: identify navigation links (SACRED — keep every `href`, every `<Link>` to, every route), auth state display, mobile menu toggle logic, dropdown handlers, data fetching.

Apply source's visual properties to target's Navbar:
- Replace Tailwind utility classes for colors, spacing, typography, layout
- Port scroll-triggered behavior
- Port hover states and transitions
- Port mobile menu visual design
- Preserve: every link destination, auth logic, click handlers, aria attributes, open/close state management

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

### Step 8: Port Footer Visual Shell
Same approach: extract source Footer visual properties, identify target Footer protected content, apply visual shell while preserving content, port animations/hover states.

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

## Phase 2: Home Page Porting

Work through target's home page section by section, top to bottom.

For EACH section:
1. Read source's corresponding section (match by visual purpose: hero, features, testimonials, CTA)
2. Read target's section fully — understand every prop, data fetch, content piece
3. Identify Port vs. Protect:
   - **Port:** Tailwind classes, CSS custom property references, layout structure (flex/grid), animation code (GSAP, ScrollTrigger, parallax), hover handlers (purely visual), responsive classes
   - **Protect:** Text content in JSX, `href` values, `src` attributes, data fetching functions, event handlers triggering business logic, children props, conditional rendering based on data/auth state
4. Rewrite target's section:
   - Keep target's imports (data, hooks, business logic utilities)
   - Apply source's Tailwind classes to target's JSX elements
   - Apply source's layout structure
   - Wire up source's animation code to target's DOM elements
   - Keep every piece of target's text content, data binding, and logic exactly as-is
5. If source has more sections than target: only port sections with logical counterparts
6. If target has more sections than source: sections without counterpart still get Phase 1 global token changes AND receive full visual treatment using source's design system (component styles, button styles, card styles, etc.)

Verify: `npm run build` passes.

## Phase 3: All Remaining Pages

Apply the full visual design system to EVERY route in the target project:

1. **Visually complex pages** — about, services, products, portfolio, contact. Port full visual shell.
2. **Simple content pages** — legal, privacy, terms, cookies, FAQ. Apply global token changes and full visual shell if source has matching page.
3. **Auth pages** — login, register, password reset, verify email. Port FULL visual styling: form container layout, input styling, button styling, page background. Zero changes to form action handlers, validation logic, redirect URLs, auth provider config.
4. **Dashboard/protected pages (Área de Clientes, admin, etc.)** — Apply the COMPLETE visual design system from source. This means: source's colors, fonts, spacing, button styles, card styles, input styles, table styles, badge styles, icon styling, animation patterns, hover states — everything. The dashboard looks like it belongs to the same site as the source. The dashboard's data, charts, business logic, API calls, and text content are 100% preserved. Do NOT give dashboard pages "only global tokens" — they get the FULL visual treatment.
5. **Dynamic route templates** — `[slug]` pages. Port the layout template's full visual shell. Do not touch `generateStaticParams`, data fetching, or dynamic content rendering.

For each page:
- Read both source and target versions
- Apply source's full visual design system
- Preserve all target content and logic
- Run `npm run build` after each page (or group of simple pages)

## Phase 4: Asset Integration & Verification

### Step 1: Copy Decorative Assets
From extraction report's decorative asset list:
```bash
cp <source-path>/public/images/hero-bg.webp <target-path>/public/images/hero-bg.webp
cp <source-path>/public/images/noise-texture.png <target-path>/public/images/noise-texture.png
cp <source-path>/public/videos/hero-loop.mp4 <target-path>/public/videos/hero-loop.mp4
```

Create target directories as needed. Never overwrite target assets with same filename — rename source asset. Only copy DECORATIVE assets.

### Step 2: Update Asset References
Scan every `.tsx`, `.ts`, `.css` file in target for references to copied assets. Ensure every reference resolves. Fix broken paths.

### Step 3: Write Asset Manifest
Create `docs/port-design-system/asset-manifest.md` listing every copied asset: source path, target path, purpose.

### Step 4: Final Build Verification
```bash
cd <target-path> && npm run build
```
Zero TypeScript errors, zero ESLint errors, successful build.

## Phase 5: QA, Cleanup, Commit

### Visual Comparison
Use MCP Chrome DevTools if available:
- Navigate each route in target
- Full-page screenshot at 1440px and 390px
- Compare visually against source
- Check: colors match (`getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`), fonts match, Navbar matches, Footer matches, animations fire correctly, hover states work, mobile layout correct at 375px

If MCP not available: instruct developer to verify side by side.

### Content Integrity Check
- For each page, compare text content before and after
- Search git diff for changes inside `<h1>`-`<h6>`, `<p>`, `<span>`, `<a>`, `<button>`, `<label>`, `<li>`
- If ANY text changed: revert immediately

### Functional Check
- Click every navigation link — all routes resolve
- Submit visible forms — still work
- If target has auth: log in, verify protected routes work
- Browser console: zero JS errors
- Network tab: zero 404s for assets

### Cleanup
- Remove temporary files
- Ensure `docs/port-design-system/changelog.md` is complete
- Ensure `docs/port-design-system/extraction-report.md` is present
- Ensure `docs/port-design-system/asset-manifest.md` is present
- Verify `.gitignore` covers `.env*` files

### Commit and Push
If developer requests:
```bash
cd <target-path>
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: port visual design system from <source-name>

- Full visual replacement: CSS tokens, typography, colors, animations
- Ported GSAP animations, ScrollTrigger configs, Lenis smooth scroll
- Ported component visual shells (Navbar, Footer, all pages)
- Copied decorative assets
- All business logic, content, and routing preserved"
git push
```

## Edge Cases

### Source has more pages than target
Only port sections that have logical counterparts. Don't create phantom routes.

### Target has more pages than source (Área de Clientes, dashboard, etc.)
Pages without a source counterpart get the COMPLETE visual design system from source — colors, fonts, spacing, component styles, animations, hover states. They look like they belong to the source's site. They just don't get section-level porting (because there's no source section to match).

### Target uses Pages Router instead of App Router
All porting logic works the same — adjust file paths. `pages/_app.tsx` instead of `app/layout.tsx`.

### Source has Three.js / 3D scenes
Port the Three.js setup: camera, geometry, materials, lighting, animation loop, renderer. Install `three` and `@react-three/fiber` / `@react-three/drei` if not present. 3D is purely visual.

### Source and target use different component libraries
Port visual tokens globally. Apply source's visual properties to target's component library equivalents. Do NOT replace target's component library.

### Source uses React 18, target uses React 19 (or vice versa)
Adapt API differences. Animation code still works. Watch for deprecated patterns.

### A source component is too tangled with logic
Port what you can cleanly extract: Tailwind classes, CSS custom property references, animation timings. Document limitations in changelog. Don't break target's logic.

## What NOT to Do

1. **Don't edit text content.** Not a single heading, paragraph, button label, link text, alt attribute, or placeholder. STOP.
2. **Don't touch `app/api/` or `pages/api/`.** Forbidden.
3. **Don't modify server actions.** `'use server'` files are off-limits.
4. **Don't change database schemas, ORM models, or migrations.**
5. **Don't alter `.env` files or any environment variable configuration.**
6. **Don't modify auth configuration.** NextAuth, Clerk, Supabase Auth — all untouchable.
7. **Don't change form action handlers or validation logic.**
8. **Don't alter URL routing.** Don't rename pages, don't change dynamic segments.
9. **Don't remove target dependencies.** Only add.
10. **Don't replace target components wholesale.** Modify their visual properties.
11. **Don't copy source components verbatim.** They contain source-specific text and routes.
12. **Don't modify test files.**
13. **Don't change CI/CD configs** (unless necessary for new visual dependency).
14. **Don't skip the build check.** After every phase, `npm run build` must pass.
15. **Don't port content images.** Only decorative assets.
16. **Don't assume source's routing structure.** Port the design system, not the information architecture.
17. **Don't give partial treatment to any page.** Every page in the target gets the full visual design system — home, products, Área de Clientes, dashboard, login, legal — ALL of them. There is no "this page only gets global tokens."
